simple.meaning: כָּרֻתָה (kâruthâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something cut , i.e. a hewn timber.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 6:36. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּרֻתָה (H3773) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: כָּרֻתָה (kâruthâh) / H3773 is traced through 1 Kings 6:36, 1 Kings 7:2, 1 Kings 7:12 with generated occurrence evidence.

structuredEvidence.definition: something cut , i.e. a hewn timber

firstOccurrence.englishText: He built the inner court with three courses of cut stone and a course of cedar beams.

timeline.evidenceText: He built the inner court with three courses of cut stone and a course of cedar beams.

For he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon. Its length was one hundred cubits,* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.
The great court around had three courses of cut stone, and a course of cedar beams; like the inner court of Yahweh’s house and the porch of the house.
